objects.label: Buon fresco versus secco
objects.text: AR.O.A1.1.1 Buon fresco versus secco. Pigment bound by lime as plaster sets, versus pigment applied to dry plaster with a binder.

objects.label: Oil glazing
objects.text: AR.O.A1.1.2 Oil glazing in fifteenth-century Netherlandish panels.

objects.label: Lost-wax casting
objects.text: AR.O.A1.1.3 Lost-wax casting. A wax model is invested, melted out and replaced by metal.

objects.label: Pentimento
objects.text: AR.O.A1.1.4 Pentimento. A change of composition visible under the paint layer.

objects.label: Dendrochronological date of a panel
objects.text: AR.O.A1.1.5 Dendrochronological date of a panel. A felling date is a lower bound on the painting date. It holds only if the board's outer rings survive or sapwood is estimated. The method's chronology is EA (uses EA, UNVERIFIED cell id).

objects.label: Whakairo technique
objects.text: AR.O.A1.1.6 Whakairo technique. Māori carving technique, as a making claim. See T/p2_ANZSRC45.md.

objects.label: Workshop attribution grades
objects.text: AR.O.A1.2.1 Workshop attribution grades. "Rembrandt", "studio of", "circle of", "follower of".

objects.label: Rembrandt Research Project
objects.text: AR.O.A1.2.2 Rembrandt Research Project (1968–2014) as an attribution programme (UNVERIFIED dates; from the prototype's link, not rechecked).

objects.label: Stylometric attribution
objects.text: AR.O.A1.2.3 Stylometric attribution. An authorship claim supported by function-word frequencies. The model is CS's; the attribution is here.

objects.label: Whakairo lineage of training
objects.text: AR.O.A1.2.4 Whakairo lineage of training. Which carving school trained a carver.

objects.label: Tuning and temperament of a performance
objects.text: AR.O.A1.3.1 Tuning and temperament of a performance. Twelve-tone equal temperament divides the octave into twelve equal frequency ratios of 2^(1/12). The ratio fact uses MA; that a named instrument was so tuned is here.

objects.label: Figured bass
objects.text: AR.O.A1.3.2 Figured bass. A notation the performer realizes in chords.

objects.label: Labanotation record
objects.text: AR.O.A1.3.3 Labanotation record (Laban, 1928) of a named choreography.

objects.label: Stemma and copy-text
objects.text: AR.O.A1.3.4 Stemma and copy-text. Lachmann's stemma assumes descent by copying with shared errors. Greg's copy-text rationale (1950) chooses the text for accidentals. Each yields a claim about the authorial reading.

objects.label: Historically informed performance claims
objects.text: AR.O.A1.3.5 Historically informed performance claims. Example: the extent of continuous vibrato in eighteenth-century string playing. CONTESTED; the alternative reads treatises as prescriptive, not descriptive.

objects.label: Meter and prosody
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.1 Meter and prosody. Iambic pentameter; quantitative meter; the mora in Japanese verse.

objects.label: Tonality
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.2 Tonality. A hierarchy of pitches around a tonic, with functional harmony. Twelve-tone serialism (Schoenberg, early 1920s) is an alternative system.

objects.label: Raga and maqam
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.3 Raga and maqam as melodic-modal systems.

objects.label: Sonata form (textbook model)
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.4 Sonata form (textbook model). Abstracted from existing works by Reicha (1826), Marx (1845) and Czerny (1848). Koch (1793) described it by modulation. It is an analytic model, not a rule composers followed.

objects.label: Linear perspective
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.5 Linear perspective. A central projection onto a plane. It assumes one fixed eye, a planar picture surface and straight light paths. Under these, parallel lines not parallel to the plane meet at a vanishing point. The projective geometry uses MA; the pictorial system is here. Brunelleschi (c. 1415–20) and Alberti, *De pictura* (1435).

objects.label: Focalization
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.6 Focalization (Genette, 1972): who sees versus who speaks. Free indirect discourse.

objects.label: Fabula and syuzhet
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.7 Fabula and syuzhet (Russian Formalists): story order versus telling order.

objects.label: Continuity editing and montage
objects.text: AR.O.A2.1.8 Continuity editing and montage in film.

objects.label: Genre as formal definition

objects.label: Style as shared formal traits

objects.label: Program music

objects.label: Publication history

objects.label: Premiere and performance history
objects.text: AR.O.A4.2.3 Premiere and performance history. The 1913 Paris premiere of *The Rite of Spring*.

objects.label: Horizon of expectations; implied reader
objects.text: AR.O.A4.3.1 Horizon of expectations (Jauss, 1967) and the implied reader (Iser, 1972).

objects.label: Influence and borrowing as dated facts
objects.text: AR.O.A4.3.2 Influence and borrowing as dated facts. Joyce's use of the *Odyssey*. Bloom's anxiety of influence (1973) is a contested theory of it.

objects.text: AR.O.A4.3.3 Distant reading (Moretti, 2000). Counts over a corpus as reception evidence. The corpus model is CS's.

objects.text: AR.O.A4.3.4 Genre as history. The Gothic novel's emergence and audience.

objects.text: AR.O.A4.4.2 Critics' polls as data. The *Sight and Sound* poll, decennial since 1952. The result is here; each ballot is AR.O.A5.2.

objects.label: Prize jury reasons; poll ballot

Art and architectural history (including technical art history and conservation science)
Performance and screen studies (theatre, dance, film, television, new media)

sections.governing_thought: Arts and literature is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Its objects are claims about five aspects of the work: medium and making, form, meaning, context and reception, and value.
sections.key_line:
- **Logic.** Inductive.
- **Plural noun.** aspects of the work.
- **Dimension.** What feature of the work the sentence is about.
- **Order.** Structural, from the material object outward to judgment.

1. Medium and making
2. Form
3. Meaning
4. Context and reception
5. Value

**MECE test.** Exclusive: a sentence about arrangement (A2) does not assert what the work represents (A3). A reception fact (A4) does not assert worth (A5). Exhaustive: a sentence naming none of the five is about the perceiver's mind (MS), the material's chemistry (CH), a structure's stability (EN), or the concept of art (PL). Each is refused by rule (section 9).
sections.assignment_rules:
1. **The work is not a claim.** A score, novel, painting or film is a substrate. Only sentences about works are filed.
2. **Medium is a substrate.** Music, painting, verse and film name bridges, never Face O cells.
3. **Direction of evidence decides arts versus history.** If the past is evidence for the work, the sentence is AR. If the work is evidence for the past, it is HI. "The contract required ultramarine" is AR.O.A4.1. "Guild records show pigment prices rising" is HI or EC.
4. **Value divides with philosophy at generality.** What merit is, and which properties confer it on any work, is PL.O.A4.4. Applying a stated criterion to named works is AR.O.A5.
5. **Valued is not valuable.** That a work is canonical, sold or polled is AR.O.A4. That it ought to be is AR.O.A5.
6. **Response mechanism is mind.** How perceivers process works in general is MS.O.A1. That a named work was received in a named way is AR.O.A4.3.
7. **Structure stays in engineering.** Whether a shell or vault stands is EN.O.A1. Its form and meaning are AR.O.A2 and AR.O.A3.
8. **Material identity stays in chemistry.** That a pigment is lead-tin yellow type I is CH.O.A1. That this panel used it is AR.O.A1.1, which uses CH.O.A1.
9. **The language system is linguistics.** English stress phonology is LN.O.A1. The metrical scheme of a poem is AR.O.A2.1. A poem's syntax as a fact of the language is LN.O.A2.
10. **Markets, rights and rule are elsewhere.** Prices and auction effects are EC.O.A2. Copyright and moral rights are LA.O.A2.2. Censorship as an act of authority is PO; its effect on the work is AR.O.A4.2.
11. **Sacred art splits.** An icon's form and making are AR. Its veneration and theological status are RE.O.A3.1. The ruling of Nicaea II (787) is an RE·T sentence.
12. **Style labels split.** "Baroque" as shared formal traits is AR.O.A2.1. "Baroque" as a span of dates is HI.O.A2. CONTESTED.
13. **No miscellaneous bucket.** Non-Western forms are filed by aspect. Raga is AR.O.A2.1; rasa is AR.O.A3.3; a haka's performance is AR.O.A1.3.
14. **Built environment (gap claim absorbed).** Design to a stated use is EN. Its aesthetic verdict is AR.O.A5. Its site is EA; its price is EC.
15. **Cited results.** Equal-temperament ratios and projective geometry use MA (uses MA.O.A2, UNVERIFIED cell). Stylometric models use CS. Dendrochronological chronology uses EA.

sections.crosswalk:
**Authority 1: LCC classes M, N, P** (LoC outlines, as checked in the prototype). 30 subclasses: M 3 (M, ML, MT); N 8 (N, NA, NB, NC, ND, NE, NK, NX); P 19 (P, PA–PM twelve, PN, PQ, PR, PS, PT, PZ).

| Subclass(es) | Lands | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| M | Refused | Holds scores, which are works: substrate |
| ML | Lands, split | Most of ML lands across AR.O.A1–A5. Music trade → EC; philosophy → PL; acoustics → PH; physiology → MS/MD |
| MT | Lands | Theory → AR.O.A2.1; instruction → AR.B.C7 |
| N, NB, NC, ND, NE, NK, NX | Land | Medium subclasses map to AR.B.C2 and AR.B.C6; their claims to Face O |
| NA | Lands, split | Structural parts → EN |
| P | Refused | Philology and linguistics → LN |
| PA–PM (12) | Land, split | Literature parts → AR.B.C1; language parts → LN |
| PN, PQ, PR, PS, PT | Land | PN1993–1999 film and PN2000–3307 theatre → AR.B.C4 |
| PZ | Refused | Holds fiction, which is works: substrate |

**Coverage: 27 of 30 subclasses land** (13 wholly, 14 split). 3 refused: M and PZ hold works; P holds linguistics. Dance (GV1580–1799.4) also lands, in AR.B.C4. LCC BH (aesthetics) → PL.O.A4.4.

**Authority 2: ANZSRC 2020 Division 36, Creative arts and writing** (checked: https://researchonline.jcu.edu.au/view/subjects/360000.html). Seven groups; 3699 is a residual and is not a cell.

| Group | Lands in |
|---|---|
| 3601 Art history, theory and criticism | AR.B.C2; theory of value parts → PL.O.A4.4 |
| 3602 Creative and professional writing | Creative writing → AR.B.C5. Professional and technical writing → LN.O.A4 (UNVERIFIED fit). Split |
| 3603 Music | AR.B.C3, AR.B.C7 |
| 3604 Performing arts | AR.B.C4, AR.B.C8 |
| 3605 Screen and digital media | AR.B.C4, AR.B.C8; media as institution → MS or PO |
| 3606 Visual arts | AR.B.C2, AR.B.C6 |

**Coverage: 6 of 6 substantive groups land** (5 wholly, 1 split). 3699 is a residual. Literary studies sits outside Division 36, at ANZSRC 4705 in Division 47 (4705 confirmed (checked 9 Oct 2026, ABS anzsrc2020_for.xlsx)). It lands in AR.B.C1; the rest of Division 47 is LN.

**Secondary checks (from the prototype, not recounted).** MLA International Bibliography, 5 coverage areas: literature, dramatic arts and folk literature land; linguistics → LN; folklore splits (belief and ritual → RE.O.A3 and MS). Getty AAT, 7 facets: 6 land in cells (Materials, Activities, Physical Attributes → AR.O.A1.1; Agents → AR.O.A1.2; Styles and Periods → AR.O.A2.1 or HI.O.A2; Associated Concepts → AR.O.A3, AR.O.A5 or PL); Objects is substrate. RILM top-level list: OPEN (not verified).

No authority class needed a new Face O cell.
sections.validation:
**Sizes.** Key line 5. Face O cells 21 (5 A-level, 16 sub-cells: A1 3, A2 2, A3 4, A4 4, A5 3). Named objects 55 (outside the cell count; each shares its sub-cell's W row). M roles 5. Heuristics 9 (outside count). W rows 21. B bridges 8.

**Key-line members, word for word.** Medium and making. Form. Meaning. Context and reception. Value.

**R7.** The governing thought and the key line name the same five members in the same order. The second governing-thought sentence uses "and value" as list grammar only.

**Open problems (R6).**
- OPEN: the warrant of practice-as-research. Is a made work evidence (W8), an experiment (W3), or neither?
- OPEN: the full RILM top-level classes and their landing.
- OPEN: the ANZSRC 4705 group number and the 3602 professional-writing split.

**Contested placements (R6).**
- CONTESTED: style labels. AR.O.A2.1 as traits; alternative HI.O.A2 as dates.
- CONTESTED: Affektenlehre. AR.O.A3.2 as code; alternative AR.O.A3.3 as expression.
- CONTESTED: historically informed performance claims (AR.O.A1.3.5). Alternative: the treatise is prescriptive, so the claim is A2.1 norm, not A1.3 practice.
- CONTESTED: Sistine restoration judgment (AR.O.A5.3.2). Alternative: the secco question is a material fact, AR.O.A1.1, before any verdict.
- CONTESTED: the golden-section heuristic (AR.M.H3). Alternative: once measured, it becomes an AR.O.A2.2 claim.
- CONTESTED: ethnomusicology's society claims. Alternative home MS.O.A5 is adopted; some practitioners would keep them in AR.
